title: Make neutrino astronomy capable of routinely resolving hidden cosmic sources

concept.text: The innovation would turn neutrino astronomy into a routine way to characterize individual cosmic sources: identify the objects producing neutrinos, measure how their emission varies with energy, and follow how it changes over time. Here, resolving a source means reliably distinguishing and associating its neutrino emission with an individual object; it does not necessarily mean producing a spatial image of that object. The intended advance extends beyond a few detections or associations to useful measurements across a varied population.

The proposed capability combines particle detection, reconstruction of event directions and energies, separation of astrophysical signals from atmospheric backgrounds, and statistical association with candidate sources. Its observations could then be compared with electromagnetic measurements and other available messengers. The title preserves the ambition to investigate hidden sources, but the supplied evidence establishes the source-characterization problem more directly than it establishes the physical advantage of observing electromagnetically obscured environments.

significance.text: Routine source-level neutrino measurements could make neutrinos a practical probe of cosmic particle acceleration. Spectra and variability would provide more discriminating evidence about source models than a detection alone, while comparisons with electromagnetic activity could test when and where energetic processes occur. Tidal disruption events illustrate the scientific motivation: the September 2026 report describes their extreme environments as possible accelerators of particles to very high energies, making them candidate neutrino sources.

Synthesis: the revolutionary step would be the transition from establishing that cosmic neutrino emission exists to using repeated, source-specific measurements to compare physical mechanisms across populations. This would resemble the opening of a productive observing channel, but it would not guarantee the imaging detail, source counts or temporal coverage available in electromagnetic astronomy. Its scientific reach would depend on source brightness, abundance, variability and the reliability of associations.

A further conditional possibility is investigating energetic regions from which electromagnetic radiation cannot readily escape. That prospect remains part of the concept, but neither supplied reviewed article establishes the relevant opacity and neutrino-escape physics. The evidence gap limits the strength of this particular impact claim; it does not demonstrate that the capability is impossible or undermine the broader case for routine neutrino source characterization.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is obtaining enough reliably attributed signal events to measure useful spectra and time histories for many individual sources. Atmospheric muons and neutrinos complicate signal identification, and uncertain directions and energies complicate reconstruction and association. The 2023 Galactic report documents the background challenge and the value of improved event selection and reconstruction. The 2026 tidal-disruption-event analysis illustrates the combined inference problem by fitting spatial, energy and timing information to distinguish signal from background.

Engineering and analysis would therefore need to improve useful-event retention, reconstruction and sensitivity together. More candidate events help only insofar as backgrounds and association uncertainties remain controlled; an apparent excess alone does not supply a detailed spectrum or a reliable time history. The reviewed material supports these observational barriers but does not specify a sufficient detector design, required exposure or quantitative performance threshold.

The earlier explanation attributed sparse detections to neutrinos' weak interactions. The supplied reviewed texts do not explicitly establish that physical premise or quantify the scarcity of events attributable to individual sources. It remains an unverified explanatory premise within this record, rather than a rejected claim. The directly documented obstacle is extracting sufficiently informative source signals from backgrounds using direction, energy and timing.

current_state.text: IceCube's June 29, 2023 report announced neutrino emission from the Milky Way. It described atmospheric backgrounds as a major observational challenge and identified finding specific sources within the Galaxy as a next step. Detecting Galactic emission is therefore an important achievement, but it is distinct from routinely attributing that emission to individual Galactic objects and measuring their spectra and variability.

The September 9, 2026 IceCube report states that the observatory had identified two galaxies as neutrino sources and observed neutrinos from the Milky Way. The two-galaxy count is a dated statement in that report, not an independently established exhaustive census through November 2026. These achievements demonstrate individual extragalactic source identification and Galactic emission, while the supplied reports do not demonstrate routine, detailed spectra and time histories across a varied population.

The same September 2026 report describes a search for neutrino emission associated with tidal disruption events, using directional and temporal associations together with event-energy information. It reports no detected emission from the search and upper limits on the contribution of these events to the diffuse neutrino flux. This constrains the tested emission possibilities; it does not establish that every tidal disruption event produces no neutrinos. The report describes the underlying work as a submitted paper, and the supplied review does not establish its subsequent publication status.

The evidence available here consists of two complete, untruncated IceCube news articles as described in the supplied review. The 2023 underlying paper was listed by DOI but had no retained artifact and was not inspected in that review. The 2026 underlying paper and numerical plots were also not inspected, so no numerical upper limits or detailed sensitivity figures can be supplied from this record. These limits concern the evidence available for this account and do not negate the reported observations.

The latest substantive supplied report is dated September 9, 2026. Although the source index records retrieval on November 11, 2026, the supplied freshness-search record is empty. Consequently, these materials support dated achievements and a bounded comparison with the proposed capability, rather than an exhaustive assessment of the field through November 1 or November 11, 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently verified observations should yield source-resolved spectra and time evolution for a varied population of individual objects, with enough information to discriminate among stated source models and compare neutrino activity with other messengers. A few isolated associations would not satisfy this proposed population-level scope. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Verified spectra and variability distinguish models across diverse sources

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: define population diversity, energy coverage, temporal resolution, measurement uncertainties and model-discrimination targets before assessing completion. Demonstrations should quantify background contamination, association ambiguity and the effects of event-selection and reconstruction choices. A credible result should show that source spectra and variability remain supported under reasonable alternative analyses, rather than depending on a single favorable analysis choice.
completion_criteria.label: Source spectra and variability survive reasonable alternative analyses

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirements: provide sufficient event information, detector-response characterization and analysis methods for independent verification, subject to stated access constraints. Replication with independent observations or instruments where feasible would strengthen the result. Repeated useful measurements should establish that the capability operates across the declared source population and observing conditions.
completion_criteria.label: Independently verifiable repeated measurements establish declared source population coverage

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report which source brightnesses, durations, sky regions and source classes the demonstration covers, including nondetections and upper limits. Finite observations would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not the ability to resolve every cosmic source. Any specific claim to characterize electromagnetically hidden regions should additionally establish why the selected regions are obscured and why the associated neutrino measurements probe them.
completion_criteria.label: Report observational boundaries and substantiate claims about hidden regions

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: AST-12, Directly detect the cosmic neutrino background, shares the neutrino messenger but has a different target and success condition. AST-09 concerns characterizing individual astrophysical sources through their emission; AST-12 concerns detecting the cosmic neutrino background. Success in either would not by itself complete the other.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-10, Open the millihertz gravitational-wave sky as a working observatory, shares the ambition of making a messenger into a routine astronomical observing capability. AST-05, Detect and identify a primordial gravitational-wave background, instead targets identification of a particular background. These efforts could contribute complementary observations, but neither gravitational-wave objective supplies the source-resolved neutrino spectra and time histories required here.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-07, Discover a reproducible breakdown of general relativity near black holes, and AST-13, Establish how the earliest massive black holes formed and grew, could overlap with AST-09 when relevant objects produce measurable neutrino emission. Such observations could inform energetic processes around those objects, but source characterization alone would establish neither a failure of general relativity nor the formation history of the earliest massive black holes.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-03, Identify the physical constituent of astronomical dark matter, and AST-14, Establish the physical energy budget of coronal heating, could benefit from relevant neutrino constraints if suitable models and detectable signals exist. The supplied evidence establishes neither connection as an achieved application. Their success conditions concern identifying a constituent or explaining an energy budget, whereas AST-09 concerns a broadly useful observational capability.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-08, Produce resolved surface maps of rocky exoplanets, illustrates an important distinction in the word resolved. AST-08 requires spatial information across a planetary surface; AST-09 requires distinguishing emission from individual cosmic sources and characterizing it. AST-01, Establish that an exoplanet hosts life, and AST-02, Detect an independently verifiable extraterrestrial technology, remain separate discovery goals without a demonstrated connection in the supplied evidence.

Roster-based synthesis: AST-04, Establish the physical cause of cosmic acceleration; AST-06, Map the cosmic dark ages and first luminous structures in three dimensions; and AST-11, Identify the first generation of metal-free stars, address different cosmological explanations, maps and populations. The supplied record does not establish routine neutrino source characterization as a route to completing those goals. All roster entries therefore retain their distinct identities and completion conditions.

unresolved_issues: Technical support for the weak-interaction explanation and the resulting source-event scarcity is absent from the supplied reviewed texts.
The physical conditions under which neutrinos could characterize electromagnetically obscured sources, and which populations would be observable, remain unestablished in this record.
No detector design, exposure requirement or quantitative performance target is supplied for routine population-level source characterization.
Population diversity, precision, temporal resolution and model-discrimination thresholds still need operational definitions; the completion criteria here are proposals.

The underlying 2023 DOI paper was not captured or inspected in the supplied review, and the 2026 underlying paper and numerical plots were not inspected. Numerical upper limits and subsequent publication status remain unresolved.
The dated two-galaxy statement and supplied reports do not establish an exhaustive state of the field through November 2026.

The review's recommendation to remove the weak-interaction premise entirely was not adopted literally: it was retained with an explicit evidence qualification to preserve the research explanation without presenting it as verified.

brief.title: Routine tracking of hidden sources in space
possible: Astronomers could routinely identify cosmic objects through neutrinos, particles arriving from space. They could measure the particles’ energies and track how each object’s emission changes over time, across many kinds of source.
why: These measurements would help astronomers distinguish competing explanations for how cosmic objects accelerate particles. Comparing neutrino activity with light from the same objects could reveal when and where those energetic processes occur.

sources.showed: A search found no neutrino emission associated with stars being torn apart by black holes. It placed limits on their contribution to the overall cosmic neutrino signal. The underlying study was reported as submitted for publication.
sources.quote: The nondetection of neutrino emission sets upper limits on the contribution from TDEs to the diffuse neutrino flux
sources.cited_for: The search shows how particle directions, energies and arrival times can test whether particular objects produce neutrinos.
sources.not_established: The search did not detect these sources or measure how their neutrino emission changes with energy and time.

sources.showed: IceCube detected high-energy neutrino emission from the Milky Way. Improved analysis separated cosmic signals from particles produced in Earth’s atmosphere.
sources.quote: A neutrino counterpart has now been measured, thus confirming what we know about our galaxy and cosmic ray sources
sources.cited_for: Galactic neutrino emission is detectable despite the atmospheric background.
sources.not_established: Detecting emission from the Galaxy does not identify its individual sources or provide their detailed energy patterns and time histories.

sources.showed: This paper reports the observation of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way.
sources.cited_for: It supports the detection of Galactic neutrino emission.
sources.not_established: Galactic emission alone does not establish routine measurements of individual objects.

shown: IceCube has identified individual galaxies as neutrino sources and detected emission from the Milky Way. These achievements establish that cosmic neutrino sources can be found; routine measurements of their energy patterns and changes over time across a varied population remain beyond them.
missing: Many individual sources still need enough reliably attributed neutrinos to reveal their energy patterns and changes over time.
Measurements need better particle directions and energies while keeping atmospheric contamination and mistaken source matches under control.
Claims about hidden regions need evidence that light cannot readily escape them and that the detected neutrinos probe those regions.

milestones.label: Varied sources yield measurements that distinguish competing explanations
milestones.explanation: Independently verified measurements would have to reveal energy patterns and changes over time across varied sources, alongside other observations. This would let astronomers distinguish competing explanations.

milestones.label: Source measurements survive alternative analyses
milestones.explanation: Results would have to survive reasonable alternative analyses under predefined coverage and precision goals, with contamination and source ambiguity quantified. This would establish that analysis choices do not drive the findings.

milestones.label: Repeated measurements establish independently verifiable population coverage
milestones.explanation: Repeated measurements would have to cover the declared source population, with enough particle data, detector characterization and methods for independent checks. This would establish that the capability works repeatedly.

milestones.label: Observational limits and hidden-region claims are established
milestones.explanation: Results would have to state coverage by brightness, duration, sky region and source type, including nondetections, and substantiate hidden-region claims. This would define the demonstrated reach.

uncertain: Which regions block escaping light yet could be studied through neutrinos remains unresolved.
The detector design and observing time needed for routine measurements across many sources remain unspecified.
The required source diversity, energy coverage, timing detail and ability to distinguish explanations still need agreed definitions.

page.title: High-energy neutrino source astronomy
page.definition: Individual cosmic objects are identified through high-energy neutrinos, electrically neutral particles with energies above 1 TeV (10¹² electronvolts), and their emission is measured across source classes. Measurements resolve energy spectra, the flux versus particle energy, and light curves, the flux versus time.

goal.need: IceCube’s 2022 analysis placed the contributions of NGC 1068 and TXS 0506+056 at no more than about 1% of the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux in their respective energy ranges. A search of 89 tidal disruption events, stars torn apart by black holes, found no signal; the 9 September 2026 announcement described submitted work, not a peer-reviewed result. Source spectra and timing test particle acceleration, including in environments that absorb gamma rays.

completion.title: Neutrino spectra and time histories are measured for individual objects in at least two source classes.
completion.criterion: Identify individual objects in at least two physically distinct astrophysical source classes through neutrino detections exceeding 5σ after correction for search trials. For those objects, measure energy spectra and emission versus time, with uncertainties, using repeated observations; resolve the time profiles of variable emission. Publish these measurements in peer-reviewed papers. Two classes is the Atlas’s minimum interpretation of population breadth; no numerical precision or cadence requirement is established.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; an operational definition assembled from published science objectives, without an externally adopted completion standard.
completion.basis: Searches of the IceCube-Gen2 science white paper, Astro2020 panel reports and P5 recommendations for a population-level source-characterization test found no required source count, spectral precision or time resolution. The criterion combines their source-class, spectrum and transient-emission goals with the field’s 5σ discovery convention. Its breadth and measurement requirements are Atlas definitions, not an adopted community standard.

milestones.title: A neutrino telescope rejects an atmospheric-only origin for its high-energy events above 5σ.
milestones.criterion: Reject the hypothesis that atmospheric muons and neutrinos explain the observed high-energy event population, exceeding the field’s 5σ discovery threshold. IceCube’s 2014 analysis met this test with 37 candidates collected over 988 live days, with deposited energies from 30 to 2,000 TeV; the atmospheric-only hypothesis was rejected at 5.7σ.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics discovery convention, documented by the Nobel Committee for Physics and applied in IceCube’s published astrophysical-flux analysis.

milestones.title: A candidate neutrino source exceeds 5σ locally and 4σ after a search of 110 selected objects.
milestones.criterion: In IceCube’s a priori catalogue-search protocol, a candidate has a local significance of at least 5σ and remains above 4σ after accounting for 110 tested sources. The 2022 NGC 1068 result met it: 5.2σ locally and 4.2σ after trials, with a fitted excess of 79 (+22/−20) events. Its power-law spectral index was 3.2 ± 0.2 statistically, with systematic uncertainty 0.07; the measurement was mainly constrained by neutrinos from 1.5 to 15 TeV.
milestones.set_by: IceCube Collaboration, the a priori 110-object catalogue-search protocol in its NGC 1068 paper; this threshold applies to that search design.
milestones.threshold_quote:
a local 5 σ detection will yield a final result above 4 σ after
accounting for trials.

milestones.title: Neutrino emission attributable to an individual cosmic object exceeds 5σ after search trials.
milestones.criterion: A spatial excess attributable to an individual object exceeds 5σ after correction for the relevant search trials. Extended Galactic emission alone does not establish this attribution. The Nobel Committee’s review dated 6 October 2026 reports Galactic emission at 5.7σ from 12 years of data, with no individual Galactic point sources identified; it describes NGC 1068 and the archival TXS 0506+056 flare at 4.2σ and 3.5σ, respectively.
milestones.set_by: Particle-physics source-discovery convention, documented by the Nobel Committee for Physics in its 2026 scientific background.

milestones.title: Multiple neutrino flares from a population of blazars exceed 5σ and yield source spectra.
milestones.criterion: Detect multiple neutrino flares from a population of blazars above 5σ and characterize their neutrino spectra, following the IceCube-Gen2 blazar science objective and its discovery benchmark. A blazar is an active galactic nucleus whose jet points near Earth. The archival TXS 0506+056 analysis found a fitted excess of 13 ± 5 events between September 2014 and March 2015, at 3.5σ after search corrections; it did not meet the discovery benchmark.
milestones.set_by: IceCube-Gen2 observatory programme, science white paper Section 3.2.1 and Figure 12; the published objective is specifically for blazars.
milestones.threshold_quote: The larger astrophysical neutrino samples provided by IceCube-Gen2 will enable definitive detection of multiple neutrino flares from a population of blazars.
